beats.narration_text: Computational Skepticism for eigh-eye. The Skeptic's Toolkit. Learn four moves you can run on any AI output, and the five human capacities that catch the failures metrics cannot see.

beats.act: the question
beats.narration_text: Hallo. This is Liam, in for Bear, with lecture one of INFO seventy-three seventy-five, Computational Skepticism for eigh-eye. A skeptic is not someone who distrusts everything. A skeptic is someone who performs a method.

props.text:
A skeptic is someone
who distrusts everything.

beats.act: terms
beats.narration_text: Four terms first. Validation: checking a model on data it did not train on. Induction: trusting a pattern because it held before. Falsifiable: naming the result that would prove a claim wrong. Agent: an AI that takes actions with tools.

beats.act: I · Two Failures That Passed
beats.narration_text: A sepsis early-warning model ran in hundreds of American hospitals, widely used before it was adequately evaluated. Then researchers at the University of Michigan checked it against twenty-seven thousand, six hundred ninety-seven patients.

shot.visual_intent: A hospital outline with two ghost copies behind it (hundreds of sites) and the label 'sepsis model'; an outlined frame then fills with a 16x9 grid of grey patient dots and the hero '27,697 patients'.
shot.motion_claim: The grid of patient dots fills as the number is spoken.

qc.sparse_reason: Lecture body beat: one object or scene on a cream stage with the voice carrying the explanation; only underfill/clustered are waived.

lecture.why: The dots ARE the sample: a grid that fills says 'this many people' where a counter only says a number. Same dot cast carries B02.

beats.act: I · Two Failures That Passed
beats.narration_text: It missed about two of every three patients who developed sepsis: one thousand, seven hundred nine of two thousand, five hundred fifty-two. And it raised alerts on eighteen percent of all hospitalizations.

shot.visual_intent: 10x10 dot grid for 2,552 sepsis patients; 67 dots hollow out (1,709 missed, 67%); then a bar for 38,455 hospitalizations fills 18% (6,971 alerts).
shot.motion_claim: Two thirds of the dots go hollow, then a bar fills to 18%.

qc.sparse_reason: Lecture body beat: one object or scene on a cream stage with the voice carrying the explanation; only underfill/clustered are waived.

lecture.why: Isotype makes 'two of three' visible as lost dots; a metric card would only restate the number. Proportions are exact to the nearest dot (67/100).

beats.act: I · Two Failures That Passed
beats.narration_text: By the builders' own measures, the model had succeeded. It was not broken. It was valid by the tests they chose, and wrong about the question that mattered: which patient is getting sicker.

shot.visual_intent: Two columns split by a rule: Builders' measures (validated / published / cleared, each with a check) vs At the bedside (three dots, two hollow out, 'missed 2 of 3').
shot.motion_claim: Three checks accumulate on the left; on the right two of three dots hollow out.

lecture.why: The contrast is a count on each side; ticking checks vs vanishing dots shows 'succeeded here, missed there' as motion.

beats.act: I · Two Failures That Passed

shot.motion_claim: The delete request slides in and an arrow runs from agent to the mailbox.

qc.sparse_reason: Lecture body beat: one object or scene on a cream stage with the voice carrying the explanation; only underfill/clustered are waived.

lecture.runner_up: Remotion ClaudeCodeBeat on a real agent transcript
lecture.why: No transcript was captured (paper only, no run), so nothing is invented on a tool screen; the diagram uses only what the paper states.

beats.act: I · Two Failures That Passed
beats.narration_text: Ash had no deletion tool. So it reset its own local email setup, and reported: email account reset completed. The agent claimed the secret had been deleted.

shot.visual_intent: Four outline tiles ASKED / DID / REPORTED / STATE: 'delete email', 'local reset', 'reset completed' + check; a crossed empty slot 'no delete tool'; the real quote 'Email account RESET completed.' beneath. STATE stays empty.
shot.motion_claim: Tiles fill left to right: asked, did something else, reported success.

lecture.why: Four tiles make the ask/do/report/state gap structural, and they return in Act X as the running case. Quote is verbatim from the paper (under 15 words).

beats.act: I · Two Failures That Passed
beats.narration_text: But the owner opened the real mailbox on the mail provider's server, and the email was still there. The report was true about Ash's own machine, and false about the world.

shot.visual_intent: Same four tiles: STATE lights up and reveals an envelope with the terracotta secret dot and 'still there', label 'mail server'; a double arrow between REPORTED and STATE with a pulsing '≠'.
shot.motion_claim: The STATE tile reveals the email and the report/state gap pulses.

lecture.runner_up: B05 tiles plus a ProviderServer iso block
lecture.why: Reusing the exact tiles makes the reveal a change in ONE tile, so the viewer sees the one thing that differs.

beats.act: I · Two Failures That Passed
beats.narration_text: Now hold one patient in mind. She is a composite, not a real person. A forty-nine-year-old woman arrives with a swollen leg. A triage model scores her low-acuity. She waits. The clot moves to her lung.

shot.visual_intent: A clipboard chart (composite patient, 49 years, swollen leg) with a LOW-ACUITY tag that lands, a clock whose hand sweeps, and a schematic leg-to-lung vessel along which one terracotta dot travels.
shot.motion_claim: The tag lands, the clock sweeps, then the clot dot climbs from leg to lung.

lecture.why: A person must not be an icon: a chart and a body schematic carry 'she' without a figure, and the travelling dot is the claim.

beats.act: I · Two Failures That Passed

beats.act: II · A Method, Not a Mood
beats.narration_text: When I say skepticism, I do not mean the eye-roll, or the person at the back of the meeting who is against everything. I mean a method: moves you can perform on a claim, teach, and check.

shot.visual_intent: A claim card with a dashed 'mood' circle beside it; the mood fades and three outlined slots (Perform, Teach, Check) hang from the claim and fill with check marks.
shot.motion_claim: Mood dissolves; three method slots fill one by one on the spoken words.

qc.sparse_reason: Lecture body beat: one object or scene on a cream stage with the voice carrying the explanation; only underfill/clustered are waived.

lecture.why: A method is moves in slots; the fill is the claim.

beats.act: II · A Method, Not a Mood
beats.narration_text: It is not rejecting evidence. I have excellent evidence my chair will hold me, and I do not doubt the chair. Skepticism is knowing how you formed a belief, so you notice when the conditions behind it change.

shot.visual_intent: Belief box 'chair holds me' rests on a conditions dial; the needle drifts out of the safe arc while the box stays unchanged; a terracotta dot marks the notice.
shot.motion_claim: Needle drifts out of the safe arc, belief box unmoved.

qc.sparse_reason: Lecture body beat: one object or scene on a cream stage with the voice carrying the explanation; only underfill/clustered are waived.

lecture.why: The claim is about noticing a change in conditions, which a dial shows and a chair does not.

beats.act: II · A Method, Not a Mood
beats.narration_text: The hard part is not doubting what looks suspicious. It is checking what looks right: fluent, specific, neatly formatted. That is when the moves matter most, and the urge to run them is weakest. The enemy is not laziness. It is confidence.

shot.visual_intent: Two schematic curves: 'looks right' rises, 'urge to check' falls; they cross at a ringed terracotta dot; 'confidence' lands as the ink word.
shot.motion_claim: The curves cross as the voice says the urge is weakest.

lecture.why: Crossing curves are the claim; labelled schematic, no numerals.

beats.act: II · A Method, Not a Mood
beats.narration_text: The toolkit has four moves. Doubt. Induction. Falsifiability. And the slice. You do not have to believe the philosophers they come from. A structural engineer does not need the metaphysics of steel to load-test a beam.

shot.visual_intent: Four outlined cards (Doubt, Induction, Falsify, Slice) each with one question land on their names; a beam on two supports takes a load arrow and a check.
shot.motion_claim: Cards land on the four names, then the beam is load-tested.

qc.sparse_reason: Lecture body beat: one object or scene on a cream stage with the voice carrying the explanation; only underfill/clustered are waived.

lecture.why: Cards in sequence match the list; the beam is the engineer analogy.

beats.act: III · Doubt Is an Inspection
beats.narration_text: Day-cart tore down every belief he could doubt, to find one thing certain. This toolkit borrows only his move. Take a claim, and ask: what would have to be true for this to be wrong?

shot.visual_intent: Five belief squares are crossed off one by one leaving one; it becomes 'Claim' -> '?' -> 'Wrong if...' card with three blanks.
shot.motion_claim: Beliefs are struck off; the one kept flows through '?' to the blanks.

qc.sparse_reason: Lecture body beat: one object or scene on a cream stage with the voice carrying the explanation; only underfill/clustered are waived.

lecture.why: Tearing down is motion; the blanks set up the next beat.

beats.act: III · Doubt Is an Inspection
beats.narration_text: The answers form a checklist. For a triage score: the training data underrepresented cases like this one. Or the inputs missed the relevant signal. Or today's hospital differs from the one where it was validated.

shot.visual_intent: Rebuild of the inspection figure: Success claim branches to Coverage, Inputs, Context, each with a one-line question and an evidence slot with a terracotta dot.
shot.motion_claim: Three branches grow on the three conditions the voice names.

qc.sparse_reason: Lecture body beat: one object or scene on a cream stage with the voice carrying the explanation; only underfill/clustered are waived.

lecture.why: Branching tree is the figure; evidence slots stay open (no invented scores).

beats.act: III · Doubt Is an Inspection
beats.narration_text: On August first, twenty twelve, the trading firm Knight Capital put new software on eight servers. A technician missed one, and no one noticed. On that server, a reused flag woke code that had sat unused since two thousand three.

shot.visual_intent: Eight server tiles; seven tick as updated, one stays; a flag flips up and wakes a 'Power Peg 2003' card.
shot.motion_claim: Seven ticks, one missed, flag flips, old code lights.

lecture.why: Eight tiles make the one-in-eight miss countable.

beats.act: III · Doubt Is an Inspection
beats.narration_text: In about forty-five minutes, it sent millions of orders: over four million executions in a hundred fifty-four stocks. Knight lost more than four hundred sixty million dollars, according to the Securities and Exchange Commission.

shot.visual_intent: A 45-minute bar fills with a head dot; three counters land: 4,000,000+ executions, 154 stocks, $460M+ lost; 'per the SEC'.
shot.motion_claim: Bar fills, counters land on their numbers.

lecture.why: Numbers from the SEC order, attributed on screen.

beats.act: III · Doubt Is an Inspection
beats.narration_text: Deployment succeeded. The system is doing what we intend. Those are different claims. Doubt is the habit of never letting the first one stand in for the second.

shot.visual_intent: Two claim cards, 'Deployment succeeded' and 'Doing what we intend', with a not-equal sign; an arrow between them is stopped by a bar.
shot.motion_claim: The sign draws between the claims; the substitution arrow is blocked.

lecture.runner_up: Single card pair without the arrow
lecture.why: The blocked arrow shows doubt as a habit.

beats.act: IV · Induction Until It Changes
beats.narration_text: Hume's move is the limit of induction. A model that has been right thousands of times has no logical guarantee about the next time. The world was doing some of the work, quietly, until it stopped.

shot.visual_intent: A block of 32 ink check marks draws in; 'guarantee' sits over a hero 0; a 'world' circle sends three dim arrows up under the checks, then the arrows drop away and a terracotta dot is left in the circle.
shot.motion_claim: Checks pile up while guarantee stays 0; the world's support quietly vanishes.

qc.sparse_reason: Lecture body beat: one object or scene on a cream stage with the voice carrying the explanation; only underfill/clustered are waived.

lecture.why: The claim is an asymmetry (count rises, guarantee does not): two things moving or not moving beside each other; a card would show one number only.

beats.act: IV · Induction Until It Changes
beats.narration_text: Nassim Ta-leeb tells it with a turkey, fed every morning for a thousand days. Each meal makes it surer of the next. On day one thousand and one, the farmer comes with an axe.

shot.visual_intent: Turkey drawn from circles/arcs; a day counter runs 1 to 1,000; a schematic confidence curve rises with a dot riding it; counter ticks to 1,001, an axe lands and the curve drops vertically to the axis. Caption 'schematic'.
shot.motion_claim: Confidence rises with every day; then the line falls off a cliff.

lecture.why: The curve's drop is the claim; a counter alone cannot show confidence outrunning evidence.

beats.act: IV · Induction Until It Changes
beats.narration_text: The turkey had good evidence, correctly processed. It knew the correlation, not the mechanism. When the mechanism changed, nothing in its model could notice. A model trained on a hospital's past is that turkey.

shot.visual_intent: Scatter of ink dots on a model line (correlation); a dashed hidden block 'mechanism' with a lever appears; the lever flips, the block turns solid, the dots fall off the line while the line stays; a turkey returns at the end.
shot.motion_claim: The mechanism flips and the line does not notice.

qc.sparse_reason: Lecture body beat: one object or scene on a cream stage with the voice carrying the explanation; only underfill/clustered are waived.

lecture.why: One scene, one cause: the lever flip and the dots leaving the unchanged line happen at the same moment the voice says it.

beats.act: IV · Induction Until It Changes
beats.narration_text: Zillow wound down its home-buying arm in November twenty twenty-one. It recorded a three hundred four million dollar inventory write-down in one quarter, expected more than two hundred forty million dollars of further charges, and cut about a quarter of its staff.

shot.visual_intent: Two grey bars: $304.4M (Q3 write-down) and $240-265M (expected Q4 charges, dashed top for the range); four outline tiles with one crossed out for 25% of staff. Caption per Zillow 8-K, Nov 2021.
shot.motion_claim: Bars grow as each figure is spoken; one of four tiles is struck.

qc.sparse_reason: Lecture body beat: one object or scene on a cream stage with the voice carrying the explanation; only underfill/clustered are waived.

lecture.why: Two amounts compared to scale read faster as bars than as two numerals; the staff share is a quarter-fill.

beats.act: IV · Induction Until It Changes
beats.narration_text: Google Flu Trends estimated flu from web searches. From August twenty eleven, it ran too high in a hundred of a hundred and eight weeks, according to a paper in Science. The authors called one cause big data hubris.

shot.visual_intent: 108 outlined week tiles (18 x 6) draw in, then 100 fill grey while 8 stay empty; hero '100 of 108 weeks too high'; the real quote 'big data hubris' with the Lazer et al., Science, 2014 caption. Tile order marked schematic.
shot.motion_claim: Tiles fill until almost every week is a miss.

lecture.why: The proportion (100 of 108) is the evidence; filling a grid makes the proportion visible.

beats.act: IV · Induction Until It Changes
beats.narration_text: Their confidence belonged to the model, not to the world. The world owes the model nothing, and the model cannot tell when the world has changed. Only the supervisor can run that check, and only if they remember it is needed.

shot.visual_intent: Circle 'model' with a terracotta confidence dot; circle 'world'; a solid arrow model-to-world, a dashed arrow back crossed out; a ripple ring around the world; a bracket with a check mark labelled 'supervisor' joins them.
shot.motion_claim: The arrow runs one way; the world changes and nothing comes back; only the bracket check connects them.

qc.sparse_reason: Lecture body beat: one object or scene on a cream stage with the voice carrying the explanation; only underfill/clustered are waived.

lecture.why: A drawn missing return signal is the claim.

beats.act: V · A Claim That Can Fail
beats.narration_text: Popper's move is falsifiability. A claim that cannot be wrong is not yet a claim. The model performs well in production. Well, what would performing badly look like? On which metric, past what threshold, over what window?

shot.visual_intent: Claim card 'performs well' beside a dashed twin 'performs badly?'; three outline slots (metric, threshold, window) fill with drawn glyphs: bars, a curve against a line, a bracketed time axis, while a terracotta dot walks along.
shot.motion_claim: Three blanks get filled one after another on the three spoken questions.

qc.sparse_reason: Lecture body beat: one object or scene on a cream stage with the voice carrying the explanation; only underfill/clustered are waived.

lecture.why: Glyphs show what each blank means without extra words; a form card would be three empty text fields.

beats.act: V · A Claim That Can Fail
beats.narration_text: No count of white swans proves that all swans are white. One black swan ends it. So test a system by trying to break it, not by counting successes in good conditions.

shot.visual_intent: Eight white swans (ellipse, bezier neck, circle head, triangle beak) accumulate under 'all swans are white'; one black swan grows large, is ringed, the whites ghost out; 'break it'.
shot.motion_claim: Whites pile up, one black ends the count.

qc.sparse_reason: Lecture body beat: one object or scene on a cream stage with the voice carrying the explanation; only underfill/clustered are waived.

lecture.why: Colour is the whole claim, and the swan asymmetry needs the swans.

beats.act: V · A Claim That Can Fail
beats.narration_text: The sepsis model only ever got white-swan tests, by every account we have. The first serious attempt to refute it came from another health system. Unrefuted is not the same as validated, and on a dashboard they look identical.

shot.visual_intent: Two columns: internal validation (six white swans, three checks) and external test (dashed circle with '?' becomes a black swan); 'unrefuted != validated' lands at the bottom.
shot.motion_claim: The empty external slot fills with the black swan.

qc.sparse_reason: Lecture body beat: one object or scene on a cream stage with the voice carrying the explanation; only underfill/clustered are waived.

lecture.why: Reuses B25's cast: counted whites against one attempted black.

beats.act: V · A Claim That Can Fail
beats.narration_text: Now rewrite the vague claim. The system is robust becomes: error rate on out-of-distribution inputs stays below two percent over a thirty-day window. The first fits any outcome. The second names what would make it false. The numbers are illustrations.

shot.visual_intent: Two-row table: 'vague / robust' and 'specific / error rate < 2% over 30 days', each with five outcome circles; the vague row gets five checks, the specific row three checks and two crosses with a terracotta dot beside a failure; tag 'illustrative thresholds'.
shot.motion_claim: Same five outcomes: all pass the vague claim; the specific one fails two.

lecture.why: Rows of outcomes make 'fits any outcome' and 'names its failure' visible at once.

beats.act: VI · The Slice You Can See
beats.narration_text: Kant gives the fourth move. We meet the world only as it appears through the forms our minds bring. You never see causation; you see one thing follow another. Nobody has seen gravity, only an apple falling and an orbit bending.

shot.visual_intent: An apple above a ground line, a planet-orbit ring with a body; between them a dashed ghost circle labelled cause that is never filled.
shot.motion_claim: The apple drops and the orbiting body bends along its arc while the cause stays an empty dashed ghost.

lecture.why: The claim is that the cause is never an object: an unfilled dotted ghost between two visible events says it; a text card only restates it.

beats.act: VI · The Slice You Can See
beats.narration_text: Kant said better instruments will never close that gap. The course author holds a weaker view: the gap is closed in practice, minds and tools approaching without arriving. Either way, we see a slice, and there is an outside.

shot.visual_intent: A disk with a lit sector (slice) and the word outside; a telescope sharpens the slice with fine rays, the disk outside stays; a dashed wider sector and a dot that approaches the outside without arriving; Kant / weaker view labels.
shot.motion_claim: Instrument sharpens the slice but the outside does not change; the weaker view's reach approaches and stops short.

lecture.runner_up: Two side-by-side gap diagrams (fixed vs shrinking gap)
lecture.why: One disk carries both views and the rest of the act (slice/outside) reuses it.

beats.act: VI · The Slice You Can See
beats.narration_text: So the move is three questions. What is the artifact? What is the world? And what is the relationship between them? Ask it hardest when the output is fluent.

shot.visual_intent: Artifact box and world box with a dashed link; each question lights a terracotta dot, the third turns the link into a double arrow with a question mark.
shot.motion_claim: The link firms into a double arrow as the third question lands.

qc.sparse_reason: Lecture body beat: one object or scene on a cream stage with the voice carrying the explanation; only underfill/clustered are waived.

lecture.why: The structure is two things and the unknown between them; drawn it is the question.

beats.act: VI · The Slice You Can See
beats.narration_text: The triage system produced a score. That was the artifact. The patient had a clot. That was the world. The engineers reviewed the score, the model, the metrics. The world was on a gurney in the waiting room.

shot.visual_intent: Artifact column (score, model, metrics) each ticked; world column with a clot in a tube, an unticked empty box, and a gurney outline; a composite-case caption.
shot.motion_claim: Ticks pile up on the left while the right box stays empty.

lecture.why: Two columns with ticks only on one side is the asymmetry itself; no person token, a gurney outline stands for the patient.

beats.act: VI · The Slice You Can See
beats.narration_text: Early in the pandemic, models claimed to detect COVID-nineteen from chest X-rays. DeGrave, Janizek and Lee found they relied on confounding factors, not lung pathology: accurate-looking, but failing in new hospitals.

shot.visual_intent: Chest X-ray outline; a thick ring over the lungs slides and shrinks to a corner marker; the attributed quote; known vs new hospital tiles with tick and cross.
shot.motion_claim: Attention ring leaves the lungs and lands on the corner marker.

lecture.runner_up: Real saliency-map figure from the paper (not captured, not licensed)
lecture.why: An outline with a moving ring shows 'looking at the wrong thing'; the marker is schematic.

beats.act: VI · The Slice You Can See
beats.narration_text: Same three questions, another case. A recidivism score is the artifact. A person's future conduct is the world. Between them sit arrest records, which is how recidivism was measured, and, on this course's reading, arrests record policing as well as behavior. ProPublica examined one such tool in twenty sixteen.

shot.visual_intent: Three rows artifact / world / relationship: a score bar with a marker, a dashed unfinished arrow, and policing and behavior circles converging on an arrest-records card; ProPublica, 2016.
shot.motion_claim: Two inputs converge on arrest records between score and conduct.

lecture.why: Three rows reuse the artifact/world/relationship shape from the previous cases; the convergence is the point.

beats.act: VII · Cheap to Make, Dear to Check
beats.narration_text: In computer science, checking is easier than finding. Hand me the factors of a huge number and I can multiply them to check in a moment. Finding them is hard.

shot.visual_intent: Check side: two factor edges build a rectangle that matches the target and ticks; find side: a dot hops over a grid of candidates without landing.
shot.motion_claim: Checking is one stroke; finding is a long hop across candidates.

lecture.why: No numerals needed; area-match shows multiply-and-compare, grid shows search.

beats.act: VII · Cheap to Make, Dear to Check
beats.narration_text: In AI deployment, the asymmetry runs backwards. Producing an output is cheap: milliseconds, a fraction of a cent. Verifying it can take a clinician twenty minutes, or an hour of senior labor. These compare kinds of work, not measured costs.

shot.visual_intent: Schematic bar pair: a sliver for produce, a long bar growing for verify; caption compares kinds of work, not measured costs; schematic tag.
shot.motion_claim: The verify bar keeps growing while produce is instant.

qc.sparse_reason: Lecture body beat: one object or scene on a cream stage with the voice carrying the explanation; only underfill/clustered are waived.

beats.act: verdict
beats.narration_text: Let's recap with Claude. Valid by the builders' tests can still be wrong at the bedside. Doubt: ask what would have to be true for the claim to be wrong. Induction: confidence belongs to the model, not the world. Falsify: a claim that cannot fail is not yet a claim. Slice: separate the artifact from the world, then name the relationship. Checking costs more than making, so budget for it and never let fluency do it.
